events.title: The last hour
events.text: Seven days of bombardment end in an hour of it. At 6.25 the final barrage begins on the German trenches from Gommecourt to the Somme, 'an incessant roar of gun-fire'. Thirteen British divisions of the Fourth Army and of the Third Army's VII Corps stand in their trenches along 25 km of front, with the French XX Corps on their right.

sources: Brig.-Gen. Sir James E. Edmonds, Military Operations France and Belgium, 1916, vol. I, Sir Douglas Haig's Command to the 1st July: Battle of the Somme (London: Macmillan, 1932), chapters XII to XIX and the order of battle: the official history, written from the war diaries.

Wikipedia, "First day on the Somme" and its pages on the capture of Montauban, Mametz, Fricourt and La Boisselle, the Gommecourt salient, the Schwaben Redoubt, the Leipzig Salient, the Hawthorn Ridge Redoubt, the mines, the Royal Newfoundland Regiment, the 31st Division and the Thiepval Memorial, for the times and German losses they quote from Edmonds, Sheldon and Whitehead.
The Long, Long Trail, the orders of battle of the 4th, 7th, 8th, 17th, 18th, 21st, 29th, 30th, 32nd, 34th, 36th, 46th and 56th Divisions, and "Time on the Western Front".
